For each window of size W (default 3) over deletable nodes, try all 2^W - 1 non-empty deletion patterns. Uses a budget limit (default 200 tests) to bound effort.

4. `reduction/vulcan/__init__.py` exporting the reducers.

5. Experiment snippet (`run_snippets/vulcan_1minimality.sh`): Vulcan experiments that run [PersesReducer + all Vulcan reducers] on bug1/bug2/bug3 (use ReductionDriver with reducers [PersesReducer(), IdentifierReplacementReducer(), SubtreeReplacementReducer(), LocalExhaustiveReducer()] and a fresh PropertyTester per bug), reporting VULCAN_BUGn_TOKENS, VULCAN_BUGn_TESTS, VULCAN_BUGn_RATIO for n=1,2,3.

When done, report: files created, test results, snippet metrics output, and any caveats.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a subagent to handle a task. The subagent runs as a same-process loop instance with its own context and wire file. Delegating also keeps the bulk of intermediate file contents out of your own context — you get a conclusion back instead of a pile of dumps.

Writing the prompt:
- The subagent starts with zero context — it has not seen this conversation. Brief it like a colleague who just walked into the room: state the goal, list what you already know, hand over the specifics.
- Lookups (read this file, run that test): put the exact path or command in the prompt. The subagent should not have to search for things you already know.
- Investigations (figure out X, find why Y): give the question, not prescribed steps — fixed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.
- Do not delegate understanding. If the task hinges on a file path or line number, find it yourself first and write it into the prompt.

Usage notes:
- When the task continues earlier work a subagent already did, prefer resuming that agent (pass its `resume` id) over spawning a fresh instance — the resumed agent keeps its prior context.
- A subagent's result is only visible to you, not to the user. When the user needs to see what a subagent produced, summarize the relevant parts yourself in your own reply.
- Subagents use a fixed 2-hour timeout. If one times out, resume the same agent instead of starting over.

When NOT to use Agent: skip delegation for trivial work you can do directly — reading a file whose path you already know, searching a small known set of files, or any task that takes only a step or two. Delegation has a context-handoff cost; it pays off only when the task is substantial enough to outweigh it.

Once a subagent is running, leave that scope to it: do not redo its searches or reads in parallel, and do not abandon it midway and finish the job manually. Both undo the context savings the delegation was meant to buy.


When `run_in_background=true`, the subagent runs detached from this turn. The completion arrives in a later turn as a synthetic user-role message containing its result — you do not need to poll, sleep, or check on its progress. Continue with other work or respond to the user. Never fabricate or predict what the result will say.

Default to a foreground subagent (omit `run_in_background`) when your next step needs its result — foreground hands the result straight back. Reach for `run_in_background=true` only when you have other work to do while it runs and do not need its result to proceed. Never launch in the background and then immediately wait on it (with `TaskOutput block=true`, sleeping, or otherwise): that just blocks the turn for no benefit — run it in the foreground instead.


Available agent types (pass via subagent_type):
- plan: Read-only implementation planning and architecture design. Use this agent when the parent agent needs a step-by-step implementation plan, key file identification, and architectural trade-off analysis before code changes are made.
  Tools: Glob, Grep, Read
- agent: Default Kimi Code agent
  Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, Write, Skill, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode, CreateGoal, GetGoal, SetGoalBudget, UpdateGoal, AgentSwarm, TaskList, TaskOutput, TaskStop, Agent, AskUserQuestion, Edit, TodoList
- coder: General software engineering agent — the only subagent type with file-editing tools; use it for any delegated task that must modify code. Use this agent for non-trivial software engineering work that may require reading files, editing code, running commands, and returning a compact but technically complete summary to the parent agent.
  Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read, Write, Skill, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode, AgentSwarm, TaskList, TaskOutput, TaskStop, Agent, Edit, TodoList
- explore: Fast codebase exploration with prompt-enforced read-only behavior. Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (e.g. "src/**/*.yaml"), search code for keywords (e.g. "database connection"), or answer questions about the codebase (e.g. "how does the auth module work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions. Use this agent for any read-only exploration that will clearly require more than 3 search queries. Prefer launching multiple explore agents concurrently when investigating independent questions.
  Tools: Bash, Glob, Grep, Read

prompt.description: Full task prompt for the subagent

description.description: Short task description (3-5 words) for UI display

subagent_type.description: One of the available agent types (see "Available agent types" in this tool description). Defaults to "coder" when omitted.

resume.description: Optional agent ID to resume instead of creating a new instance. When set, do not also pass subagent_type — the resumed agent keeps its own type, and supplying both is rejected.

run_in_background.description: If true, return immediately without waiting for completion. Prefer false unless the task can run independently and there is a clear benefit to not waiting.

model.description: Which model to run the subagent on: "secondary" = the configured secondary model; "primary" = the main model you are running on (for hard, quality-sensitive tasks). This explicit choice overrides the selected agent type's model_preference; without either, secondary is the default when configured. Only effective when a secondary model is configured; otherwise the subagent inherits your model. Ignored when resuming — resumed subagents keep their own model.

tools.name: AgentSwarm
tools.description:
Launch multiple subagents from one prompt template, existing agent resumes, or both.

Use AgentSwarm when many subagents should run the same kind of task over different inputs. The placeholder is exactly `{{item}}`. For example, with `prompt_template` set to `Review {{item}} for likely regressions.` and `items` set to `["src/a.ts", "src/b.ts"]`, AgentSwarm launches two new subagents with those two concrete prompts. For a few differently-shaped tasks, make separate `Agent` calls in one message instead.

Use `resume_agent_ids` to continue subagents that already exist from earlier work, such as ones that failed or timed out: map each agent id to the prompt for that resumed subagent (usually `continue` if no extra information is needed). You may combine `resume_agent_ids` with `items` in the same call to resume existing subagents and launch new ones. Do not duplicate resumed work in `items`.

Each of these is enforced — a violation is rejected before any subagent starts: provide at least 2 `items` unless you pass `resume_agent_ids`; whenever `items` are present, `prompt_template` is required and must contain `{{item}}`; and the filled-in prompts must be distinct (two items that expand to the same prompt are rejected).

Use enough subagents to keep the work focused and parallel. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents, and launches are queued automatically, so it is safe to split large tasks into many clear, independent items.

If `AgentSwarm` is called, that call must be the only tool call in the response.

description.description: Short description for the whole swarm.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type used for every new subagent spawned from items; defaults to coder when omitted. Resumed subagents always keep their original type, so passing subagent_type together with resume_agent_ids is allowed — it only affects the item-based spawns.

prompt_template.description: Prompt template for each subagent. The {{item}} placeholder is replaced with each item value.

items.description: Values used to fill {{item}}. Each item launches one new subagent.

resume_agent_ids.description: Map of existing subagent agent_id to the prompt used to resume that subagent. These resumed subagents are launched before new item-based subagents.

model.description: Which model to run the item-spawned subagents on: "secondary" = the configured secondary model; "primary" = the main model you are running on (for hard, quality-sensitive tasks). This explicit choice overrides the selected agent type's model_preference; without either, secondary is the default when configured. Only effective when a secondary model is configured; otherwise subagents inherit your model. Resumed subagents always keep their own model.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Execute a `bash` command. Use this for shell semantics — pipes, env, processes, git, package managers, build/test runners, anything genuinely interactive or multi-step.

**Translate these to a dedicated tool instead:**
- `cat` / `head` / `tail` (known path) → `Read`
- `sed` / `awk` (in-place edit) → `Edit`
- `echo > file` / `cat <<EOF` → `Write`
- `find` / recursive `ls` to locate files by name pattern → `Glob` (plain `ls <known-directory>` is fine for listing a directory)
- `grep` / `rg` (search file contents) → `Grep`
- `echo` / `printf` (talk to the user) → just output text directly

The dedicated tools render in the per-tool permission UI and keep raw stdout out of the conversation; that is why they are worth reaching for whenever one fits.

**Output:**
The stdout and stderr will be combined and returned as a string. The output may be truncated if it is too long. If the command exits non-zero, the output ends with a `Command failed with exit code: N` line; a command killed by its timeout or interrupted by the user ends with its own message instead.

If `run_in_background=true`, the command will be started as a background task and this tool will return a task ID instead of waiting for command completion. When doing that, you must provide a short `description`. Background commands default to a 600s timeout and `timeout` is capped at 86400s; set `disable_timeout=true` only when the task should run without a timeout. You will be automatically notified when the task completes. After starting one, default to returning control to the user instead of immediately waiting on it. Use `TaskOutput` only for a non-blocking status/output snapshot — do not set `block=true` to wait for a task you just launched, since its completion arrives automatically; reserve `block=true` for when the user explicitly asked you to wait. Use `TaskStop` only if the task must be cancelled. If a human user wants to inspect background tasks themselves, point them to the `/tasks` command, which opens an interactive panel; it has no subcommands.

**Guidelines for safety and security:**
- Each shell tool call will be executed in a fresh shell environment. The shell variables, current working directory changes, and the shell history is not preserved between calls. To run a command in a particular directory, pass the `cwd` argument (or use absolute paths) rather than relying on a `cd` from an earlier call.
- The tool call will return after the command is finished. You shall not use this tool to execute an interactive command or a command that may run forever. For possibly long-running foreground commands, set the `timeout` argument in seconds. Foreground commands default to 60s and allow up to 300s. When a foreground command hits its timeout it is moved to the background instead of being killed, and you will be automatically notified when it completes.
- Avoid using `..` to access files or directories outside of the working directory.
- Avoid modifying files outside of the working directory unless explicitly instructed to do so.
- Never run commands that require superuser privileges unless explicitly instructed to do so.

**Guidelines for efficiency:**
- Use `&&` to chain commands that genuinely depend on each other, e.g. `npm install && npm test`. Independent read-only commands (separate `git show`, `ls`, or status checks) should be issued as separate parallel Bash calls in one response, not chained into a single call — chaining serializes their execution and mixes their output. Do not stitch outputs together with `echo` separators.
- Use `;` to run commands sequentially regardless of success/failure
- Use `||` for conditional execution (run second command only if first fails)
- Use pipe operations (`|`) and redirections (`>`, `>>`) to chain input and output between commands
- Always quote file paths containing spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "/path with spaces/")
- Compose multi-step logic in a single call with `if` / `case` / `for` / `while` control flows.
- Prefer `run_in_background=true` for long-running builds, tests, watchers, or servers when you need the conversation to continue before the command finishes.

**Commands available:**
The following common command categories are usually available. Availability still depends on the host, so when in doubt run `which <command>` first to confirm a command exists before relying on it.
- Navigation and inspection: `ls`, `pwd`, `cd`, `stat`, `file`, `du`, `df`, `tree`
- File and directory management: `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `ln`, `chmod`, `chown`
- Text and data processing: `wc`, `sort`, `uniq`, `cut`, `tr`, `diff`, `xargs`
- Archives and compression: `tar`, `gzip`, `gunzip`, `zip`, `unzip`
- Networking and transfer: `curl`, `wget`, `ping`, `ssh`, `scp`
- Version control: `git`; for GitHub-hosted work (PRs, issues, CI runs, API queries) prefer the `gh` CLI when installed — it carries the user's GitHub auth and can return structured JSON
- Process and system: `ps`, `kill`, `top`, `env`, `date`, `uname`, `whoami`
- Language and package toolchains: `node`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `python`, `pip` (use whichever the project actually relies on)

cwd.description: The working directory in which to run the command. When omitted, the command runs in the session's working directory.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds for the command to execute. Foreground default 60s, max 300s. Background default 600s, max 86400s. Ignored for background commands when disable_timeout=true.

description.description: A short description for the background task. Required when run_in_background is true.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run the command as a background task.

disable_timeout.description: If true, do not apply a timeout to the command. Only applies when run_in_background is true.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Perform exact replacements in existing files.

- Edit is mandatory for every incremental change, especially small edits. DO NOT use Write or Bash `sed`.
- Read the target file before every Edit. DO NOT call Edit from memory, stale context, or a guessed `old_string`.
- Take `old_string` and `new_string` from the Read output view.
- Drop the line-number prefix and tab; match only file content.
- `old_string` must be unique unless `replace_all` is set.
- If `old_string` is ambiguous, add surrounding context. Use `replace_all` only when every occurrence should change — for example, renaming a symbol throughout the file.
- Multiple Edit calls may run in one response only when they do not target the same file.
- DO NOT issue consecutive Edit calls on the same file. A previous Edit can invalidate a later Edit's `old_string`, causing `old_string not found`. Read the file again before the next Edit.
- A write lock serializes same-file edits in response order, but serialization does not make stale `old_string` valid.
- For pure CRLF files, Read shows LF; use LF in `old_string` and `new_string`, and Edit writes CRLF back.
- For mixed endings or lone carriage returns, Read shows carriage returns as \r; include actual \r escapes in those positions.

path.description: Path to the text file to edit. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute.

old_string.description: Exact content to replace from the Read output view, without the line-number prefix. Use LF for pure CRLF files; use actual \r escapes where Read shows \r.

new_string.description: Replacement text in the same Read output view. LF is written back as CRLF only for pure CRLF files.

replace_all.description: Set true only when every occurrence of old_string should be replaced.

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task.
Getting user sign-off on your approach via ExitPlanMode before writing code prevents wasted effort.

Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. New Feature Implementation - e.g. "Add a caching layer to the API"
2. Multiple Valid Approaches - e.g. "Optimize database queries" (indexing vs rewrite vs caching)
3. Code Modifications - e.g. "Refactor auth module to support OAuth"
4. Architectural Decisions - e.g. "Add WebSocket support"
5. Multi-File Changes - involves more than 2-3 files
6. Unclear Requirements - need exploration to understand scope
7. User Preferences Matter - if user input would materially change the implementation approach, use EnterPlanMode to structure the decision

Permission mode notes:
- EnterPlanMode enters plan mode automatically without an approval prompt in all permission modes.
- In yolo and manual modes, ExitPlanMode still presents the plan to the user for approval.
- In auto permission mode, do not use AskUserQuestion; make the best decision from available context.
- In auto permission mode, ExitPlanMode exits plan mode without asking the user.
- Use EnterPlanMode only when planning itself adds value.

When NOT to use:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- User gave very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks

Once you are in plan mode, a reminder walks you through the workflow (explore → design → write the plan file → `ExitPlanMode`) and enforces read-only access. For non-trivial tasks where you are unsure of the codebase structure or relevant code paths, use `Agent(subagent_type="explore")` to investigate first when the `Agent` tool is available.

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode reminder.
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it reads the plan from the file you wrote.
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it. In auto permission mode, the tool reads the file and exits plan mode without asking the user.

## When to Use
Only use this tool for tasks that require planning implementation steps. For research tasks (searching files, reading code, understanding the codebase), do NOT use this tool.

## What a good plan contains
List specific, verifiable steps grounded in the actual codebase — real files, functions, and commands, in a sensible order. Each step should be concrete enough to act on and to check. Avoid vague filler like "improve performance" or "add tests"; say what to change and where.

## Multiple Approaches
If your plan offers multiple alternative approaches, pass them via the `options` parameter so the user can choose which one to execute — see the `options` parameter for the format, count, and reserved labels. In yolo and manual modes the user sees all options alongside the host's Reject and Revise controls.

## Before Using
- In auto permission mode, do NOT use AskUserQuestion; make the best decision from available context.
- In auto permission mode, this tool exits plan mode without asking the user.
- In yolo and manual modes, this tool still presents the plan to the user for approval.
- If auto permission mode is not active and you have unresolved questions, use AskUserQuestion first.
- If auto permission mode is not active and you have multiple approaches and haven't narrowed down yet, consider using AskUserQuestion first to let the user choose, then write a plan for the chosen approach only.
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval.
- Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan OK?" or "Should I proceed?" - that is exactly what ExitPlanMode does.
- If rejected, revise based on feedback and call ExitPlanMode again.

options.description: When the plan contains multiple alternative approaches, list them here so the user can choose which one to execute. Provide up to 3 options; 2-3 distinct approaches work best when the plan offers a real choice. Passing a single option is allowed and is equivalent to a plain plan approval. Each option represents a distinct approach from the plan. Do not use "Reject", "Revise", "Approve", or "Reject and Exit" as labels.

label.description: Short name for this option (1-8 words). Append "(Recommended)" if you recommend this option.

description.description: Brief summary of this approach and its trade-offs.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Search file contents using regular expressions (powered by ripgrep).

Use Grep when the task is to find unknown content or unknown file locations. Do not use shell `grep` or `rg` directly; this tool applies workspace path policy, output limits, and sensitive-file filtering.
ALWAYS use Grep tool instead of running `grep` or `rg` from a shell — direct shell calls bypass workspace policy, output limits, and sensitive-file filtering.
If you already know a concrete file path and need to inspect its contents, use Read directly instead.

Write patterns in ripgrep regex syntax, which differs from POSIX `grep` syntax. For example, braces are special, so escape them as `\{` to match a literal `{`.

Hidden files (dotfiles such as `.gitlab-ci.yml` or `.eslintrc.json`) are searched by default. To also search files excluded by `.gitignore` (such as `node_modules` or build outputs), set `include_ignored` to `true`. Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always skipped for safety, even when `include_ignored` is `true`.

path.description: File or directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Omit to search the current working directory. Use Read instead when you already know a concrete file path and need its contents.

glob.description: Optional glob filter for which files to search, e.g. `*.ts`. Matched against each file's full absolute path, so a path-anchored pattern like `src/**/*.ts` silently matches nothing — use a basename pattern (`*.ts`), or anchor with `**/` (`**/src/**/*.ts`). To scope the search to a directory, use `path` instead.

type.description: Optional ripgrep file type filter, such as ts or py. Prefer this over `glob` when filtering by language or file kind: it is more efficient and less error-prone than an equivalent glob pattern.

output_mode.description: Shape of the result. `content` shows matching lines (honors `-A`, `-B`, `-C`, `-n`, and `head_limit`); `files_with_matches` shows only the paths of files that contain a match, most-recently-modified first (honors `head_limit`); `count_matches` shows per-file match counts as `path:count` lines, preceded by an aggregate total line. Defaults to `files_with_matches`.

-i.description: Perform a case-insensitive search. Defaults to false.

-n.description: Prefix each matching line with its line number. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`. Defaults to true.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`; takes precedence over `-A` and `-B`.

head_limit.description: Limit output to the first N lines/entries after offset. Defaults to 250. Pass 0 for unlimited.

offset.description: Number of leading lines/entries to skip before applying `head_limit`. Use it together with `head_limit` to page through large result sets. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline matching, where the pattern can span line boundaries and `.` also matches newlines. Defaults to false.

include_ignored.description: Also search files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Read a text file from the local filesystem.

If the user provides a concrete file path to a text file, call Read directly. Do not `Glob`, `ls`, or otherwise pre-check known text file paths; missing or invalid file paths return errors you can handle. Do not use Read for directories; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob when you need files matching a name pattern (Glob lists files only, never directories). Use `Grep` only when the task is to search for unknown content or locations.

When you need several files, prefer to read them in parallel: emit multiple `Read` calls in a single response instead of reading one file per turn.

- Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute.
- Returns up to 1000 lines or 100 KB per call, whichever comes first; lines longer than 2000 chars are truncated mid-line.
- Page larger files with `line_offset` (1-based start line) and `n_lines`. Omit `n_lines` to read up to the 1000-line cap.
- Sensitive files (`.env` files, credential stores, SSH private keys, and similar secrets) are refused to protect secrets; do not attempt to read them. Templates and public keys are exempt: `.env.example` / `.env.sample` / `.env.template` and public SSH keys such as `id_rsa.pub` read normally.
- Only UTF-8 text files can be read. Non-UTF-8 encodings, binary files, and files containing NUL bytes are refused; use `ReadMediaFile` for images or video, and Bash or an MCP tool for other binary formats.
- Negative line_offset reads from the end of the file (for example, -100 reads the last 100 lines); the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.
- Output format: `<line-number>\t<content>` per line.
- A `<system>...</system>` status block is appended after the file content; it summarizes how much was read (line and byte counts, truncation, line-ending notes) and is not part of the file itself.
- Pure CRLF files are displayed with LF line endings; `Edit` matches this output and preserves CRLF when writing back.
- Mixed or lone carriage-return line endings are shown as `\r` and require exact `Edit.old_string` escapes.
- After a successful `Edit`/`Write`, do not re-read solely to prove the write landed. When the task depends on an exact file, API, or output shape, inspect the final external contract before finishing.

path.description: Path to a text file. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute. Directories are not supported; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob for pattern search.

line_offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Omit to start at line 1. Negative values read from the end of the file; the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.

n_lines.description: The number of lines to read; the tool also applies its internal cap. Omit to read up to the internal cap of 1000 lines.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description: Invoke a registered skill from the current skill listing. BLOCKING REQUIREMENT: when a skill from the listing matches the user's request, you MUST call this tool (not free-form text). Do not re-invoke a skill to repeat work already done: if a `<kimi-skill-loaded>` block for it with the same `args` is already present in the conversation, follow those instructions directly instead of calling the tool again. Do call the tool again when you need the skill with different arguments — the loaded block was expanded with the earlier `args` and will not reflect new inputs.

skill.description: The exact name of the skill to invoke, spelled as it appears in the current skill listing (e.g. "commit", "pdf").

args.description: Optional argument string for the skill, written like a command line (e.g. `-m "fix bug"`, `123`, a file path). It is split on whitespace (quotes group a token) and expanded into the skill's placeholders ($NAME, $1, $ARGUMENTS); if the skill body has no placeholders, the whole string is still appended as a trailing `ARGUMENTS:` line. Omit it only when there is nothing to pass.

tools.name: TaskList
tools.description:
List background tasks and their current status.

Use this tool to discover which background tasks exist and where each one
stands. It is the entry point for inspecting background work: it returns a
task ID, status, and description for every task it reports, plus the command,
PID, and (once finished) exit code for shell tasks, and a stop reason for any
task that ended early.

Guidelines:

- After a context compaction, or whenever you are unsure which background
  tasks are running or what their task IDs are, call this tool to
  re-enumerate them instead of guessing a task ID.

Use this after `Bash(run_in_background=true)` or `Agent(run_in_background=true)` to check progress, or to read the output of a task that has already completed.

1	"""Perses syntax-aware program reducer.
2	
3	Implements the core Perses algorithm: a priority-queue traversal of the
4	SparTree (largest subtrees first) applying two kinds of grammar-guided
5	transformations:
6	
7	- Quantifier-node reduction: for KLEENE_STAR / KLEENE_PLUS / OPTIONAL
8	  nodes, a ddmin-style partition removal over the child list.
9	- Compatible-subtree replacement: for REGULAR nodes, replacing the node
10	  with a smaller descendant that has the same rule name.
11	
12	Every candidate is validated by cloning the tree, applying the change to
13	the clone, and running the property tester on the clone's source. A
14	change is only kept when the property holds and the token count strictly
15	decreases.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	import heapq
20	import itertools
21	from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
22	
23	from reduction.tree import SparTreeNode, NodeType
24	from reduction.property_test import PropertyTester
25	from reduction.reducer import AbstractReducer
26	
27	
28	class PersesReducer(AbstractReducer):
29	    """Syntax-aware reducer based on the Perses algorithm.
30	
31	    Traverses the SparTree with a priority queue ordered by subtree token
32	    count (largest first), so big reductions are attempted before small
33	    ones. After a successful reduction of a node, its (new) children are
34	    re-queued so the traversal continues on the changed structure.
35	    """
36	
37	    @property
38	    def name(self) -> str:
39	        """The name of this reduction algorithm."""
40	        return "perses"
41	
42	    def reduce(self, tree: SparTreeNode, tester: PropertyTester) -> SparTreeNode:
43	        """Reduce the given SparTree while preserving the property.
44	
45	        Mutates and returns `tree`.
46	
47	        Args:
48	            tree: The SparTree to reduce (root node).
49	            tester: Property tester that validates reduction candidates.
50	
51	        Returns:
52	            The same tree object, mutated in place.
53	        """
54	        self._root = tree
55	        self._tester = tester
56	        self._counter = itertools.count()
57	        self._live_ids: Optional[set[int]] = None
58	
59	        heap: List[Tuple[int, int, SparTreeNode]] = []
60	        self._push(heap, tree)
61	
62	        while heap:
63	            _, _, node = heapq.heappop(heap)
64	            if not self._is_live(node):
65	                continue
66	
67	            reduced = False
68	            if node.node_type in (NodeType.KLEENE_STAR,
69	                                  NodeType.KLEENE_PLUS,
70	                                  NodeType.OPTIONAL):
71	                reduced = self._reduce_quantifier_node(node)
72	            elif node.node_type == NodeType.REGULAR:
73	                reduced = self._reduce_regular_node(node)
74	
75	            if reduced:
76	                # Structure changed: re-queue the node itself (more
77	                # reductions may apply) and invalidate the liveness cache.
78	                self._live_ids = None
79	                self._push(heap, node)
80	
81	            # Continue the traversal with the node's current children.
82	            for child in node.children:
83	                if not child.deleted:
84	                    self._push(heap, child)
85	
86	        return tree
87	
88	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
89	    # Priority queue helpers
90	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
91	
92	    def _push(self, heap: List[Tuple[int, int, SparTreeNode]],
93	              node: SparTreeNode) -> None:
94	        """Push a node onto the priority queue, largest subtree first."""
95	        count = node.token_count()
96	        if count == 0:
97	            return
98	        heapq.heappush(heap, (-count, next(self._counter), node))
99	
100	    def _is_live(self, node: SparTreeNode) -> bool:
101	        """Check whether a queued node is still part of the tree.
102	
103	        The cache is recomputed lazily whenever a reduction has mutated
104	        the tree. Heap entries hold strong references to their nodes, so
105	        id() values of stale entries cannot be reused by live nodes.
106	        """
107	        if node.deleted:
108	            return False
109	        if self._live_ids is None:
110	            self._live_ids = {id(n) for n in self._root.all_nodes()}
111	        return id(node) in self._live_ids
112	
113	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
114	    # Candidate validation
115	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
116	
117	    def _find_path(self, target: SparTreeNode) -> Optional[List[int]]:
118	        """Find the child-index path from the root to `target` (by identity)."""
119	        path: List[int] = []
120	
121	        def dfs(node: SparTreeNode) -> bool:
122	            if node is target:
123	                return True
124	            for i, child in enumerate(node.children):
125	                path.append(i)
126	                if dfs(child):
127	                    return True
128	                path.pop()
129	            return False
130	
131	        return list(path) if dfs(self._root) else None
132	
133	    def _node_at_path(self, root: SparTreeNode, path: List[int]) -> SparTreeNode:
134	        """Walk a child-index path from `root` and return the node there."""
135	        node = root
136	        for index in path:
137	            node = node.children[index]
138	        return node
139	
140	    def _try_mutation(self, node: SparTreeNode, mutate) -> bool:
141	        """Test a mutation on a cloned tree and keep it if it succeeds.
142	
143	        Clones the whole tree, applies `mutate` to the clone's counterpart
144	        of `node`, and runs the property tester on the clone's source.
145	        The mutation is applied to the real tree only when the property
146	        holds and the token count strictly decreases.
147	
148	        Args:
149	            node: The real-tree node the mutation conceptually applies to.
150	            mutate: Callable applying the change to a (cloned) node.
151	
152	        Returns:
153	            True if the mutation was accepted and applied to the real tree.
154	        """
155	        path = self._find_path(node)
156	        if path is None:
157	            return False
158	
159	        before = self._root.token_count()
160	        candidate = self._root.clone()
161	        clone_node = self._node_at_path(candidate, path)
162	        mutate(clone_node)
163	
164	        if candidate.token_count() >= before:
165	            return False
166	        if not self._tester.test(candidate.to_source()):
167	            return False
168	
169	        mutate(node)
170	        return True
171	
172	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
173	    # Quantifier-node reduction (ddmin over children)
174	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
175	
176	    def _min_children(self, node: SparTreeNode) -> int:
177	        """Minimum number of children a quantifier node must keep."""
178	        return 1 if node.node_type == NodeType.KLEENE_PLUS else 0
179	
180	    def _reduce_quantifier_node(self, node: SparTreeNode) -> bool:
181	        """Apply ddmin-style partition removal over a node's children.
182	
183	        Splits the child list into n partitions and tries deleting each
184	        partition group. On success, recurses on the remaining children
185	        with granularity max(n-1, 2); otherwise doubles the granularity.
186	        The single-child case is handled by trying to delete the child
187	        directly when the grammar allows an empty node.
188	
189	        Args:
190	            node: A KLEENE_STAR, KLEENE_PLUS, or OPTIONAL node.
191	
192	        Returns:
193	            True if any children were removed.
194	        """
195	        changed = False
196	        min_keep = self._min_children(node)
197	
198	        while len(node.children) > min_keep:
199	            # Single-child case: try deleting it directly when the
200	            # grammar allows the node to become empty.
201	            if len(node.children) == 1:
202	                if min_keep == 0 and node.is_deletable():
203	                    if self._try_mutation(node, lambda n: n.children.pop(0)):
204	                        changed = True
205	                break
206	
207	            n = 2
208	            progressed = False
209	            while len(node.children) > min_keep:
210	                count = len(node.children)
211	                partitions = self._split_indices(count, min(n, count))
212	                removed_partition = False
213	
214	                for start, end in partitions:
215	                    # Respect the minimum-child constraint.
216	                    if count - (end - start) < min_keep:
217	                        continue
218	                    if self._try_mutation(
219	                            node,
220	                            lambda nd, s=start, e=end: nd.children.__delitem__(slice(s, e))):
221	                        changed = True
222	                        progressed = True
223	                        removed_partition = True
224	                        n = max(n - 1, 2)
225	                        break
226	
227	                if not removed_partition:
228	                    if n >= count:
229	                        break
230	                    n = min(n * 2, count)
231	
232	            if not progressed:
233	                break
234	
235	        return changed
236	
237	    def _split_indices(self, length: int, n: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
238	        """Split a range of `length` items into n roughly equal partitions.
239	
240	        Returns:
241	            List of (start, end) index pairs.
242	        """
243	        n = max(1, min(n, length))
244	        size = length // n
245	        remainder = length % n
246	        partitions = []
247	        start = 0
248	        for i in range(n):
249	            end = start + size + (1 if i < remainder else 0)
250	            partitions.append((start, end))
251	            start = end
252	        return partitions
253	
254	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
255	    # REGULAR-node reduction (compatible-subtree replacement)
256	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
257	
258	    def _reduce_regular_node(self, node: SparTreeNode) -> bool:
259	        """Try replacing a REGULAR node with a smaller compatible descendant.
260	
261	        A descendant is compatible when it has the same rule name (so the
262	        replacement is grammar-compatible) and fewer tokens. Candidates
263	        are tried smallest-first.
264	
265	        Args:
266	            node: A REGULAR node.
267	
268	        Returns:
269	            True if a replacement was accepted.
270	        """
271	        if not node.children:
272	            return False
273	
274	        own_count = node.token_count()
275	        candidates = [
276	            desc for desc in node.all_nodes()
277	            if desc is not node
278	            and desc.node_type == NodeType.REGULAR
279	            and not desc.deleted
280	            and desc.rule_name == node.rule_name
281	            and 0 < desc.token_count() < own_count
282	        ]
283	        # Smallest candidates first: bigger reductions win early.
284	        candidates.sort(key=lambda d: d.token_count())
285	
286	        for desc in candidates:
287	            desc_path = self._find_path(desc)
288	            node_path = self._find_path(node)
289	            if desc_path is None or node_path is None:
290	                continue
291	            if not self._try_replacement(node, node_path, desc_path):
292	                continue
293	            return True
294	        return False
295	
296	    def _try_replacement(self, node: SparTreeNode,
297	                         node_path: List[int],
298	                         desc_path: List[int]) -> bool:
299	        """Test replacing the node at `node_path` by the one at `desc_path`."""
300	        before = self._root.token_count()
301	
302	        candidate = self._root.clone()
303	        clone_desc = self._node_at_path(candidate, desc_path)
304	
305	        # Replace the node with the descendant inside the cloned tree.
306	        if node_path:
307	            parent = self._node_at_path(candidate, node_path[:-1])
308	            parent.children[node_path[-1]] = clone_desc
309	        else:
310	            return False
311	
312	        if candidate.token_count() >= before:
313	            return False
314	        if not self._tester.test(candidate.to_source()):
315	            return False
316	
317	        # Apply to the real tree: move the real descendant into place.
318	        real_parent = self._node_at_path(self._root, node_path[:-1])
319	        real_desc = self._node_at_path(self._root, desc_path)
320	        real_parent.children[node_path[-1]] = real_desc
321	        return True

1	"""SparTree (Syntax-aware Parse Tree) representation for program reduction."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	from enum import Enum
5	from typing import List, Optional
6	import copy
7	
8	from reduction.token import Token
9	
10	
11	class NodeType(Enum):
12	    """Types of nodes in the SparTree, corresponding to grammar quantifiers."""
13	    KLEENE_STAR = "kleene_star"    # Zero or more repetitions
14	    KLEENE_PLUS = "kleene_plus"    # One or more repetitions
15	    OPTIONAL = "optional"          # Zero or one occurrence
16	    REGULAR = "regular"            # Exactly one occurrence (sequence/alternation)
17	    TOKEN = "token"                # Leaf node holding a token
18	
19	
20	class SparTreeNode:
21	    """A node in the SparTree parse tree.
22	
23	    The SparTree is the core data structure for syntax-aware reduction.
24	    Each node corresponds to a grammar rule, and the tree structure
25	    reflects the syntactic structure of the program. Nodes can be
26	    marked as 'deleted' to represent program variants with fewer tokens.
27	    """
28	
29	    def __init__(
30	        self,
31	        rule_name: str,
32	        node_type: NodeType,
33	        children: Optional[List['SparTreeNode']] = None,
34	        token: Optional[Token] = None,
35	    ):
36	        self.rule_name = rule_name
37	        self.node_type = node_type
38	        self.children: List[SparTreeNode] = children if children is not None else []
39	        self.token = token
40	        self.deleted: bool = False
41	
42	    def token_count(self) -> int:
43	        """Count non-deleted token descendants."""
44	        if self.deleted:
45	            return 0
46	        if self.node_type == NodeType.TOKEN:
47	            return 1
48	        return sum(child.token_count() for child in self.children)
49	
50	    def tokens(self) -> List[Token]:
51	        """Get non-deleted tokens in order (left-to-right traversal)."""
52	        if self.deleted:
53	            return []
54	        if self.node_type == NodeType.TOKEN and self.token is not None:
55	            return [self.token]
56	        result = []
57	        for child in self.children:
58	            result.extend(child.tokens())
59	        return result
60	
61	    def to_source(self) -> str:
62	        """Reconstruct source code from non-deleted tokens.
63	
64	        Rebuilds the source text by placing tokens at their original
65	        line/column positions where possible.
66	        """
67	        tokens = self.tokens()
68	        if not tokens:
69	            return ""
70	
71	        # Group tokens by line
72	        lines_dict: dict[int, list[Token]] = {}
73	        for tok in tokens:
74	            if tok.type == 'NEWLINE':
75	                continue
76	            if tok.line not in lines_dict:
77	                lines_dict[tok.line] = []
78	            lines_dict[tok.line].append(tok)
79	
80	        if not lines_dict:
81	            return ""
82	
83	        # Reconstruct lines
84	        result_lines = []
85	        for line_num in sorted(lines_dict.keys()):
86	            line_tokens = sorted(lines_dict[line_num], key=lambda t: t.col)
87	            line_str = ""
88	            current_col = 0
89	            for tok in line_tokens:
90	                if tok.type == 'INDENT':
91	                    line_str += tok.value
92	                    current_col = len(tok.value)
93	                else:
94	                    if tok.col > current_col:
95	                        line_str += " " * (tok.col - current_col)
96	                    elif current_col > 0 and line_str and not line_str.endswith(' '):
97	                        line_str += " "
98	                    line_str += tok.value
99	                    current_col = tok.col + len(tok.value)
100	            result_lines.append(line_str)
101	
102	        return "\n".join(result_lines) + "\n"
103	
104	    def clone(self) -> 'SparTreeNode':
105	        """Create a deep copy of this node and all descendants."""
106	        return copy.deepcopy(self)
107	
108	    def all_nodes(self) -> List['SparTreeNode']:
109	        """Get all non-deleted descendant nodes (including self) in pre-order."""
110	        if self.deleted:
111	            return []
112	        result = [self]
113	        for child in self.children:
114	            result.extend(child.all_nodes())
115	        return result
116	
117	    def delete(self) -> None:
118	        """Mark this node and all children as deleted."""
119	        self.deleted = True
120	        for child in self.children:
121	            child.delete()
122	
123	    def undelete(self) -> None:
124	        """Unmark deletion on this node and all children."""
125	        self.deleted = False
126	        for child in self.children:
127	            child.undelete()
128	
129	    def is_deletable(self) -> bool:
130	        """Determine if this node can be deleted per grammar rules.
131	
132	        Deletion rules:
133	        - KLEENE_STAR children: always deletable (zero or more)

from __future__ import annotations

from enum import Enum

    """Types of grammar rules."""
    SEQUENCE = "sequence"          # A B C (all in order)
    ALTERNATION = "alternation"    # A | B | C (one of)
    KLEENE_STAR = "kleene_star"    # A* (zero or more)
    KLEENE_PLUS = "kleene_plus"    # A+ (one or more)
    OPTIONAL = "optional"          # A? (zero or one)


@dataclass
class GrammarRule:
    """A single grammar production rule.

    Attributes:
        name: The non-terminal name for this rule.
        rule_type: How symbols are combined (sequence, alternation, etc.).
        symbols: List of symbol names (strings referencing other rules or terminals).
    """
    name: str
    rule_type: RuleType
    symbols: List[Union[str, 'GrammarRule']]

    def is_quantified(self) -> bool:
        """Check if this rule uses a quantifier (star, plus, optional)."""
        return self.rule_type in (RuleType.KLEENE_STAR, RuleType.KLEENE_PLUS, RuleType.OPTIONAL)


@dataclass
class Grammar:
    """A collection of grammar rules defining a language.

    Attributes:
        rules: Mapping from rule name to GrammarRule.
        start_symbol: The top-level rule name.

    start_symbol: str = "program"

        self.rules[rule.name] = rule

"""Vulcan identifier replacement reducer.

Pushes beyond 1-minimality by shrinking identifiers: long identifier
names are replaced with shorter (single-character) names. This does not
change the token count, but it reduces the program's size in characters
and can enable further structural reductions.

Each candidate rename is validated individually: the whole tree is
cloned, all occurrences of the identifier are renamed in the clone, and
the property tester is run on the clone's source. The rename is applied
to the real tree only when the property still holds.
"""

from __future__ import annotations
import string
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

from reduction.tree import SparTreeNode, NodeType
from reduction.token import KEYWORDS
from reduction.property_test import PropertyTester
from reduction.reducer import AbstractReducer


class IdentifierReplacementReducer(AbstractReducer):
    """Replace identifiers with shorter names while preserving the property.

    Unique identifier tokens are collected and sorted by frequency
    (most frequent first, ties broken alphabetically, so the behavior is
    deterministic). Each identifier is tentatively renamed to the
    shortest available single-character name; a rename is kept only if
    the property tester accepts the renamed program.
    """

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The name of this reduction algorithm."""
        return "vulcan_identifier_replacement"

    def reduce(self, tree: SparTreeNode, tester: PropertyTester) -> SparTreeNode:
        """Rename identifiers in `tree` to shorter names.

        Mutates and returns `tree`.

        Args:
            tree: The SparTree to reduce (root node).
            tester: Property tester that validates reduction candidates.

        Returns:
            The same tree object, mutated in place.
        """
        frequencies = self._identifier_frequencies(tree)
        # Names already taken: every identifier in the program plus all
        # keywords. A candidate colliding with any of these could change
        # the program's meaning, so it is never offered.
        used = set(frequencies) | KEYWORDS

        # Most frequent identifiers get the shortest names first.
        ordered = sorted(frequencies, key=lambda n: (-frequencies[n], n))

        for original in ordered:
            if len(original) <= 1:
                continue
            for candidate in self._short_names():
                if candidate in used or len(candidate) >= len(original):
                    continue
                if self._try_rename(tree, original, candidate, tester):
                    used.add(candidate)
                    break
        return tree

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _identifier_frequencies(self, tree: SparTreeNode) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """Count occurrences of each identifier token in the tree."""
        frequencies: Dict[str, int] = {}
        for node in tree.all_nodes():
            if (node.node_type == NodeType.TOKEN and node.token is not None
                    and node.token.type == 'IDENTIFIER'):
                frequencies[node.token.value] = \
                    frequencies.get(node.token.value, 0) + 1
        return frequencies

    def _short_names(self) -> List[str]:
        """Candidate single-character names, shortest/alphabetical first."""
        return list(string.ascii_lowercase) + list(string.ascii_uppercase)

    def _rename_in_tree(self, tree: SparTreeNode, original: str,
                        candidate: str) -> int:
        """Rename every `original` identifier token in `tree` to `candidate`.

        Returns:
            The number of token nodes renamed.
        """
        renamed = 0
        for node in tree.all_nodes():
            if (node.node_type == NodeType.TOKEN and node.token is not None
                    and node.token.type == 'IDENTIFIER'
                    and node.token.value == original):
                node.token.value = candidate
                renamed += 1
        return renamed

    def _try_rename(self, tree: SparTreeNode, original: str,
                    candidate: str, tester: PropertyTester) -> bool:
        """Test renaming `original` to `candidate` on a clone; keep on success."""
        clone = tree.clone()
        if self._rename_in_tree(clone, original, candidate) == 0:
            return False
        if not tester.test(clone.to_source()):
            return False
        self._rename_in_tree(tree, original, candidate)
        return True

"""Vulcan subtree replacement reducer.

Complements Perses' local (descendant-only) compatible-subtree
replacement with a global search: for each non-leaf node, any subtree
anywhere in the tree with the same rule name is a replacement
candidate, provided it is strictly smaller. The replacement is kept
only when the property is preserved and the token count decreases.

Every candidate is validated by cloning the whole tree, performing the
replacement inside the clone, and running the property tester on the
clone's source.
"""

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import List, Optional

from reduction.tree import SparTreeNode, NodeType
from reduction.property_test import PropertyTester
from reduction.reducer import AbstractReducer


class SubtreeReplacementReducer(AbstractReducer):
    """Replace nodes with smaller, rule-compatible subtrees from anywhere.

    Nodes are considered largest-first (greedy: big reductions early).
    For each node, compatible subtrees — same rule name, strictly fewer
    tokens, not the node itself and not one of its ancestors — are tried
    smallest-first. After every accepted replacement the traversal
    restarts, because the tree structure has changed.
    """

    # Upper bound on candidates tried per node, to keep the number of
    # property tests bounded on trees with many same-rule subtrees.
    MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_NODE = 10

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The name of this reduction algorithm."""
        return "vulcan_subtree_replacement"

    def reduce(self, tree: SparTreeNode, tester: PropertyTester) -> SparTreeNode:
        """Reduce `tree` by global compatible-subtree replacement.

        Mutates and returns `tree`.

        Args:
            tree: The SparTree to reduce (root node).
            tester: Property tester that validates reduction candidates.

        Returns:
            The same tree object, mutated in place.
        """
        self._root = tree
        self._tester = tester

        progress = True
        while progress:
            progress = False
            nodes = [
                n for n in tree.all_nodes()
                if n is not tree
                and n.node_type != NodeType.TOKEN
                and n.children
                and n.token_count() > 1
            ]
            # Largest subtrees first: greedy on reduction size.
            nodes.sort(key=lambda n: -n.token_count())
            for node in nodes:
                if self._try_node(node):
                    progress = True
                    break  # structure changed: restart the traversal
        return tree

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Replacement logic
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _try_node(self, node: SparTreeNode) -> bool:
        """Try replacing `node` with a smaller same-rule subtree."""
        own_count = node.token_count()
        candidates = [
            cand for cand in self._root.all_nodes()
            if cand is not node
            and cand.node_type != NodeType.TOKEN
            and cand.rule_name == node.rule_name
            and 0 < cand.token_count() < own_count
            and not self._contains(cand, node)  # no ancestor replacement
        ]
        # Smallest candidates first: bigger reductions win early.
        candidates.sort(key=lambda c: c.token_count())

        for cand in candidates[:self.MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_NODE]:
            if self._try_replacement(node, cand):
                return True
        return False

    def _contains(self, ancestor: SparTreeNode, node: SparTreeNode) -> bool:
        """Check whether `node` is a descendant of (or equal to) `ancestor`."""
        return any(n is node for n in ancestor.all_nodes())

    def _try_replacement(self, node: SparTreeNode,
                         candidate: SparTreeNode) -> bool:
        """Test replacing `node` by a copy of `candidate`; keep on success."""
        node_path = self._find_path(node)
        if node_path is None or not node_path:
            return False  # node detached, or is the root

        before = self._root.token_count()

        clone = self._root.clone()
        clone_parent = self._node_at_path(clone, node_path[:-1])
        clone_parent.children[node_path[-1]] = candidate.clone()

        if clone.token_count() >= before:
            return False
        if not self._tester.test(clone.to_source()):
            return False

        # Apply to the real tree.
        real_parent = self._node_at_path(self._root, node_path[:-1])
        real_parent.children[node_path[-1]] = candidate.clone()
        return True

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Path helpers (identity-based, mirroring the Perses reducer)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _find_path(self, target: SparTreeNode) -> Optional[List[int]]:
        """Find the child-index path from the root to `target` (by identity)."""
        path: List[int] = []

        def dfs(node: SparTreeNode) -> bool:
            if node is target:
                return True
            for i, child in enumerate(node.children):
                path.append(i)
                if dfs(child):
                    return True
                path.pop()
            return False

        return list(path) if dfs(self._root) else None

    def _node_at_path(self, root: SparTreeNode, path: List[int]) -> SparTreeNode:
        """Walk a child-index path from `root` and return the node there."""
        node = root
        for index in path:
            node = node.children[index]
        return node

"""Vulcan local exhaustive reducer.

Sliding-window exhaustive deletion: Perses' ddmin-style quantifier
reduction can miss deletion combinations that only succeed together.
This reducer slides a window of size W (default 3) over the deletable
nodes of the tree and tries all 2^W - 1 non-empty deletion patterns per
window, largest patterns first. A test budget (default 200 property
tests per invocation) bounds the effort.

Each pattern is validated by cloning the tree, marking the window's
target nodes as deleted in the clone, and running the property tester
on the clone's source. A pattern is applied to the real tree only when
the property holds and the token count strictly decreases.
"""

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import List, Optional

from reduction.tree import SparTreeNode
from reduction.property_test import PropertyTester
from reduction.reducer import AbstractReducer


class LocalExhaustiveReducer(AbstractReducer):
    """Exhaustive deletion within a sliding window over deletable nodes.

    After every accepted deletion pattern the node list is rebuilt and
    the scan restarts, because the tree structure has changed. The
    reducer stops when a full pass over all windows makes no progress or
    when the test budget is exhausted.
    """

    def __init__(self, window_size: int = 3, budget: int = 200):
        """Initialize the reducer.

        Args:
            window_size: Number of deletable nodes per window (W).
            budget: Maximum number of property tests per reduce() call.
        """
        if window_size < 1:
            raise ValueError("window_size must be >= 1")
        if budget < 1:
            raise ValueError("budget must be >= 1")
        self.window_size = window_size
        self.budget = budget

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The name of this reduction algorithm."""
        return "vulcan_local_exhaustive"

    def reduce(self, tree: SparTreeNode, tester: PropertyTester) -> SparTreeNode:
        """Exhaustively try deletion patterns within each window.

        Mutates and returns `tree`.

        Args:
            tree: The SparTree to reduce (root node).
            tester: Property tester that validates reduction candidates.

        Returns:
            The same tree object, mutated in place.
        """
        self._root = tree
        start_count = tester.test_count

        while self._within_budget(tester, start_count):
            nodes = self._deletable_nodes(tree)
            if not nodes:
                break

            progressed = False
            max_start = max(1, len(nodes) - self.window_size + 1)
            for wstart in range(max_start):
                window = nodes[wstart:wstart + self.window_size]
                if self._try_window(window, tester, start_count):
                    progressed = True
                    break  # structure changed: rebuild the node list
                if not self._within_budget(tester, start_count):
                    break

            if not progressed:
                break
        return tree

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Window / pattern logic
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _deletable_nodes(self, tree: SparTreeNode) -> List[SparTreeNode]:
        """Deletable, non-empty nodes in pre-order (root excluded)."""
        return [
            n for n in tree.all_nodes()
            if n is not tree and n.is_deletable() and n.token_count() > 0
        ]

    def _patterns(self, size: int) -> List[int]:
        """All non-empty deletion patterns over `size` nodes as bitmasks.

        Ordered by descending popcount (biggest deletions first), then by
        mask value, so the search is deterministic and greedy.
        """
        masks = range(1, 1 << size)
        return sorted(masks, key=lambda m: (-bin(m).count('1'), m))

    def _try_window(self, window: List[SparTreeNode],
                    tester: PropertyTester, start_count: int) -> bool:
        """Try every non-empty deletion pattern over `window`."""
        for mask in self._patterns(len(window)):
            if not self._within_budget(tester, start_count):
                return False
            targets = [window[i] for i in range(len(window))
                       if mask >> i & 1]
            if self._try_deletion(targets, tester):
                return True
        return False

    def _try_deletion(self, targets: List[SparTreeNode],
                      tester: PropertyTester) -> bool:

        paths = [self._find_path(t) for t in targets]

        node = root

"""Tests for the Vulcan reducers (pushing beyond 1-minimality).

Run with: python3 agent_tests/test_vulcan_1minimality.py
"""

import os
import stat
import sys
import tempfile

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))

from reduction.grammar import Grammar
from reduction.pnf import normalize_grammar
from reduction.parser import Parser
from reduction.property_test import PropertyTester
from reduction.perses_reducer import PersesReducer
from reduction.driver import ReductionDriver
from reduction.vulcan import (
    IdentifierReplacementReducer,
    SubtreeReplacementReducer,
    LocalExhaustiveReducer,
)

WORKSPACE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
BUG1_DIR = os.path.join(WORKSPACE, "test_subjects", "bug1")


def make_subject(source: str, script_body: str):
    """Create a temp dir with program.py + executable test.sh."""
    tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="vulcan_test_")
    program_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "program.py")
    script_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "test.sh")
    with open(program_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(source)
    with open(script_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(script_body)
    os.chmod(script_path, os.stat(script_path).st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)
    return program_path, script_path


def parse(source: str):
    grammar = normalize_grammar(Grammar.python_simplified())
    return Parser(grammar).parse(source)


def test_reducer_names() -> None:
    """The vulcan package must export the three reducers with names."""
    assert IdentifierReplacementReducer().name == "vulcan_identifier_replacement"
    assert SubtreeReplacementReducer().name == "vulcan_subtree_replacement"
    assert LocalExhaustiveReducer().name == "vulcan_local_exhaustive"
    print("[ok] reducer names and package exports")


def test_identifier_replacement() -> None:
    """Long identifiers must be renamed to shorter property-preserving names."""
    source = (
        "def long_function_name(argument_one):\n"
        "    return argument_one + 1\n"
        "\n"
        "result_value = long_function_name(41)\n"
        "print(result_value)\n"
    )
    program_path, script_path = make_subject(
        source, '#!/bin/bash\npython3 "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q "^42$"\n')

    tree = parse(source)
    tester = PropertyTester(script_path)
    assert tester.test(source), "subject must satisfy the property initially"

    before_chars = len(tree.to_source())
    tree = IdentifierReplacementReducer().reduce(tree, tester)
    reduced_source = tree.to_source()

    assert "long_function_name" not in reduced_source, \
        "long function identifier was not renamed"
    assert "argument_one" not in reduced_source, \
        "long parameter identifier was not renamed"
    assert len(reduced_source) < before_chars, "source did not shrink"
    assert tester.test(reduced_source), "renamed program lost the property"
    print(f"[ok] identifier replacement: {before_chars} -> "
          f"{len(reduced_source)} chars, property preserved")


def test_identifier_replacement_respects_property() -> None:
    """A rename that breaks the property must be rejected."""
    # Property: the exact identifier 'marker' must appear in the output.
    source = (
        "marker = 1\n"
        "print(marker)\n"
    )
    program_path, script_path = make_subject(
        source, '#!/bin/bash\ngrep -q "marker" "$1"\n')

    tree = parse(source)
    tester = PropertyTester(script_path)
    tree = IdentifierReplacementReducer().reduce(tree, tester)

    assert "marker" in tree.to_source(), \
        "property-breaking rename was accepted"
    print("[ok] identifier replacement rejects property-breaking renames")


def test_subtree_replacement() -> None:
    """A node must be replaceable by a smaller same-rule subtree elsewhere."""
    source = (
        "if True:\n"
        "    value = 1\n"
        "    value = 2\n"
        "if True:\n"
        "    value = 3\n"
        "print(value)\n"
    )
    program_path, script_path = make_subject(
        source, '#!/bin/bash\npython3 "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q "^3$"\n')

    tree = parse(source)
    tester = PropertyTester(script_path)
    assert tester.test(source)

    before = tree.token_count()
    tree = SubtreeReplacementReducer().reduce(tree, tester)
    after = tree.token_count()

    assert after < before, f"no subtree replacement applied ({before} -> {after})"
    assert tester.test(tree.to_source()), "replaced tree lost the property"
    print(f"[ok] subtree replacement: {before} -> {after} tokens, "
          "property preserved")


def test_local_exhaustive() -> None:
    """Window patterns must find deletions single-node ddmin can miss, bounded."""
    source = (
        "import os\n"
        "import sys\n"
        "\n"
        "def helper(x):\n"
        "    return x + 1\n"
        "\n"
        "if helper(1) > 0:\n"
        "    print('ok')\n"
        "else:\n"
        "    print('bad')\n"
    )
    program_path, script_path = make_subject(
        source, '#!/bin/bash\npython3 "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q "ok"\n')

    tree = parse(source)
    tester = PropertyTester(script_path)
    assert tester.test(source)

    budget = 50
    before = tree.token_count()
    before_tests = tester.test_count
    tree = LocalExhaustiveReducer(window_size=3, budget=budget).reduce(tree, tester)
    tests_used = tester.test_count - before_tests

    assert tree.token_count() < before, "no deletion applied"
    assert tests_used <= budget, f"budget exceeded: {tests_used} > {budget}"
    assert tester.test(tree.to_source()), "deleted tree lost the property"
    print(f"[ok] local exhaustive: {before} -> {tree.token_count()} tokens "
          f"in {tests_used} tests (budget {budget})")


def test_local_exhaustive_budget_zero_progress() -> None:
    """With an unsatisfiable property nothing may be deleted."""
    source = (
        "if True:\n"
        "    x = 1\n"
        "else:\n"
        "    x = 2\n"
        "print(x)\n"
    )
    program_path, script_path = make_subject(
        source, '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n')  # property never holds

    tree = parse(source)
    tester = PropertyTester(script_path)
    before = tree.token_count()
    tree = LocalExhaustiveReducer(window_size=3, budget=30).reduce(tree, tester)
    assert tree.token_count() == before, "deletion accepted without property"
    print("[ok] local exhaustive keeps tree intact when property never holds")


def test_vulcan_pipeline_on_bug1() -> None:
    """Full Vulcan pipeline on bug1: must beat or match Perses and keep the bug."""
    with open(os.path.join(BUG1_DIR, "program.py")) as f:
        source = f.read()

    grammar = normalize_grammar(Grammar.python_simplified())
    tester = PropertyTester(os.path.join(BUG1_DIR, "test.sh"))
    reducers = [
        PersesReducer(),
        IdentifierReplacementReducer(),
        SubtreeReplacementReducer(),
        LocalExhaustiveReducer(budget=50),
    ]
    driver = ReductionDriver(grammar, tester, reducers)
    result = driver.reduce(source)

    print(f"[..] bug1 vulcan pipeline: {result.original_tokens} -> "
          f"{result.reduced_tokens} tokens "
          f"(ratio {result.reduction_ratio:.2%}, {result.num_tests} tests)")

    assert result.reduced_tokens < result.original_tokens, "no reduction achieved"
    assert tester.test(result.reduced_source), "reduced source lost the property"
    print("[ok] Vulcan pipeline on bug1 preserves the property")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_reducer_names()
    test_identifier_replacement()
    test_identifier_replacement_respects_property()
    test_subtree_replacement()
    test_local_exhaustive()
    test_local_exhaustive_budget_zero_progress()
    test_vulcan_pipeline_on_bug1()
    print("ALL TESTS PASSED")

Done. Requirement `vulcan_1minimality` is implemented, tested, and has a verified experiment snippet.

## Files created

- `reduction/vulcan/identifier_replacement.py` — `IdentifierReplacementReducer` (name `"vulcan_identifier_replacement"`). Collects unique `IDENTIFIER` tokens with frequencies, sorts most-frequent-first (ties alphabetical, deterministic), and tries renaming each to an unused single-character name (`a`–`z`, `A`–`Z`, never colliding with existing identifiers or keywords). Each rename is validated individually: clone tree → rename in clone → property test → apply to the real tree only on success.
- `reduction/vulcan/subtree_replacement.py` — `SubtreeReplacementReducer` (name `"vulcan_subtree_replacement"`). For each non-leaf node (largest-first), searches the *whole* tree for same-`rule_name` subtrees that are strictly smaller (excluding itself and its ancestors), tries them smallest-first, capped at 10 candidates per node to bound test count. Accepted only if the property holds and token count strictly decreases; restarts the traversal after each accepted replacement.
- `reduction/vulcan/local_exhaustive.py` — `LocalExhaustiveReducer(window_size=3, budget=200)` (name `"vulcan_local_exhaustive"`). Slides a window of W deletable nodes (pre-order, root excluded) and tries all 2^W−1 non-empty deletion patterns (bitmask order: largest popcount first, then mask value — deterministic and greedy). Stops at the per-invocation test budget and when a full pass makes no progress.
- `reduction/vulcan/__init__.py` — exports all three reducers.
- `agent_tests/test_vulcan_1minimality.py` — 7 tests (names/exports, identifier rename + rejection of property-breaking renames, subtree replacement, local-exhaustive reduction + budget bound + no-progress case, full Vulcan pipeline on bug1).
- `run_snippets/vulcan_1minimality.sh` — runs `[PersesReducer(), IdentifierReplacementReducer(), SubtreeReplacementReducer(), LocalExhaustiveReducer()]` via `ReductionDriver` with a fresh `PropertyTester` per bug, in the same heredoc style as `run.sh`.

## Key design point

`SparTreeNode.to_source()` renders tokens at their original line/col, so a subtree moved across the tree lands on the wrong line (produces e.g. a body-less `if`). `SubtreeReplacementReducer._reposition` re-anchors a copied candidate's tokens to the replaced node's first-token line, preserving relative line offsets and columns — this was necessary to make cross-tree replacements work.
